source.pc: In this skill you learn to solve a system of linear equations with multiple variables. If you have two equations like and , and two target variables and , then you will be able to determine the solution for and as and . This includes solving one equation for one unknown, substituting this solution into the other equation, solving that equation, substituting this result back into the first solution and reducing the resulting fraction of fractions into a single fraction.

Suppose that we have two equations, like and . We could define two target variables (like and ) that we want to solve for, treating all other variables as constants. How would we find the solutions for and ?

The procedure of solving a system of linear equations with multiple variables is actually identical to solving a system of linear equations where there are only two variables. (So without any non-target variables.) First we pick one equation and solve it for one target variable. This gives us This is a valid solution, but it contains a fraction within a fraction which is undesirable and should be simplified. Taking the respective steps, we end up with This is as simple as we can write the solution. Now that we have solutions for and , we have solved the system of equations.

After solving a system of equations, it's always worth while to check your solution, just to make sure you haven't made an error along the way. To do so, we insert both solutions into both equations. This gives us The solution is correct if both equations always hold. To see if this is the case, we must simplify the equations. Note that all fractions have the same denominator, so we can merge the fractions together, giving Expanding brackets and canceling sum terms turns the above into We finally note that, in each of the fractions, we can pull a factor out of the brackets. This gives us Both these equations obviously hold for all values of , and , since the fractions equal and can hence be removed. As a result, we conclude that the solution we found is correct.

You may note that checking the solution is just as much work, or possibly even more, than finding the solution. As a result, as you gain more experience with this skill and learn to work thoroughly, you don't always check your results anymore. But in case of doubt, it is still a useful trick to have.
